Almost everything in this series starts from linearization, so it pays to know the linear case completely. Consider
$$
\dot x = A x, \qquad x \in \R^2, \quad A \in \R^{2 \times 2}.
$$ {#eq-linear}
Write $\tau = \tr A$ and $\Delta = \det A$. The characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^2 - \tau\lambda + \Delta$, so the eigenvalues are
$$
\lambda_{\pm} = \frac{\tau \pm \sqrt{\tau^2 - 4\Delta}}{2}.
$$ {#eq-eigenvalues}

## The classification

::: {#thm-classification}
## Trace–determinant classification
Suppose $\Delta \neq 0$, so the origin is the only equilibrium of @eq-linear. Then the origin is

1. a **saddle** if $\Delta < 0$;
2. a **node** if $\Delta > 0$ and $\tau^2 > 4\Delta$: stable if $\tau < 0$, unstable if $\tau > 0$;
3. a **spiral** if $\Delta > 0$, $\tau^2 < 4\Delta$ and $\tau \neq 0$: stable if $\tau < 0$, unstable if $\tau > 0$;
4. a **center** if $\Delta > 0$ and $\tau = 0$.

On the parabola $\tau^2 = 4\Delta$ the eigenvalues coincide and the origin is a star or degenerate node.
:::

::: {.proof}
By @eq-eigenvalues, $\lambda_+\lambda_- = \Delta$ and $\lambda_+ + \lambda_- = \tau$. If $\Delta < 0$ the eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, which gives a saddle. If $\Delta > 0$ and $\tau^2 > 4\Delta$ they are real with the same sign as $\tau$, which gives a node. If $\tau^2 < 4\Delta$ they are complex conjugates with real part $\tau/2$, so solutions rotate while growing, decaying or, when $\tau = 0$, keeping their size.
:::

@fig-trace-det draws the regions of @thm-classification, and @fig-portraits shows one phase portrait from each.

::: {#fig-trace-det}
```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "The trace-determinant plane. The parabola Delta = tau squared over 4 separates nodes from spirals, the negative Delta half-plane holds saddles, and the positive Delta axis holds centers."
tau = np.linspace(-4, 4, 400)

def draw(fig, ax, c):
    ax.plot(tau, tau**2 / 4, color=c.accent, lw=1.6)
    ax.axhline(0, color=c.fg, lw=1)
    ax.plot([0, 0], [0, 4.5], color=c.accent2, lw=1.6)
    labels = [(0, -1.4, "saddles"), (-3.2, 1.0, "stable\nnodes"), (3.2, 1.0, "unstable\nnodes"),
              (-1.2, 3.2, "stable\nspirals"), (1.2, 3.2, "unstable\nspirals"), (0.15, 4.2, "centers")]
    for x, y, s in labels:
        ax.text(x, y, s, ha="left" if s == "centers" else "center", va="center", fontsize=10)
    ax.set(xlim=(-4, 4), ylim=(-2.5, 4.5), xlabel=r"$\tau = \mathrm{tr}\,A$", ylabel=r"$\Delta = \det A$")

themed(draw)
```

The trace–determinant plane. The parabola is $\Delta = \tau^2/4$.
:::

::: {#fig-portraits}
```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "Four phase portraits: a saddle, a stable node, a stable spiral and a center."
cases = [("Saddle", [[1, 0], [0, -1]]), ("Stable node", [[-2, 0], [0, -0.5]]),
         ("Stable spiral", [[-0.3, 1], [-1, -0.3]]), ("Center", [[0, 1], [-1, 0]])]
g = np.linspace(-2, 2, 25)
X, Y = np.meshgrid(g, g)

def draw(fig, axes, c):
    for ax, (name, A) in zip(axes.flat, cases):
        A = np.array(A, dtype=float)
        U, V = A[0, 0] * X + A[0, 1] * Y, A[1, 0] * X + A[1, 1] * Y
        ax.streamplot(X, Y, U, V, color=c.accent, density=0.9, linewidth=0.7, arrowsize=0.8)
        ax.plot(0, 0, "o", color=c.fg, ms=4)
        ax.set_title(f"{name}   τ = {np.trace(A):.2g}, Δ = {np.linalg.det(A):.2g}", fontsize=10)
        ax.set(xticks=[], yticks=[], aspect="equal")

themed(draw, 2, 2, figsize=(7, 7))
```

One system from each open region of @fig-trace-det.
:::

## Hyperbolicity

The classification also says when linearization can be trusted. An equilibrium is *hyperbolic* when no eigenvalue has zero real part, and the Hartman–Grobman theorem says that near a hyperbolic equilibrium a nonlinear flow looks like its linearization.

::: {#prp-hyperbolic}
The origin of @eq-linear is hyperbolic if and only if $\Delta \neq 0$, and $\tau \neq 0$ or $\Delta < 0$.
:::

::: {.proof}
An eigenvalue is zero exactly when $\Delta = 0$. A nonzero eigenvalue is purely imaginary exactly when the eigenvalues are $\pm i\sqrt{\Delta}$, that is, when $\tau = 0$ and $\Delta > 0$.
:::

So of the regions in @fig-trace-det, only the centers (and the line $\Delta = 0$) are fragile: an arbitrarily small nonlinear term can turn a linear center into a spiral in either direction. That fragility is where the [Hopf bifurcation](../2026-08-22-hopf-bifurcation/index.qmd) lives.

## Example: the damped oscillator

::: {#exm-oscillator}
The oscillator $\ddot x + b\dot x + x = 0$ with $b \geq 0$ becomes @eq-linear with
$$
A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -b \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \tau = -b, \quad \Delta = 1.
$$
As $b$ increases from $0$ the system moves left along the line $\Delta = 1$ in @fig-trace-det. It is a center at $b = 0$, a stable spiral for $0 < b < 2$ (underdamped), and a stable node for $b > 2$ (overdamped). The critical damping $b = 2$ is where the line meets the parabola.
:::

The standard references are @strogatz2015 [ch. 5] and @hirsch2013 [ch. 4].
